notes.text: Available in cPanel 90 and later. Disabled when the WebServer role is disabled. Lists weblog analyzer settings for each domain on the selected account; no domain selector or request defaults are documented.

Only analyzers enabled for this user on the system are shown. enabled is the cumulative administrator/user setting for the domain; enabled_by_user records the user choice. These are integer 0/1 flags, with optional name, analyzers and domain fields preserved. Empty lists remain empty.

Additional analyzer settings remain in responseMeta()->uapi[metadata], separate from the returned domain list. The metadata analyzers have available_for_user, enabled_by_default and name; metadata locked=1 means only the reseller or root can manage configuration and locked=0 means the cPanel user can manage it. The metadata description is not a typed payload contract and establishes no analyzer execution behavior.

notes.text: Account-wide replacement: explicitly read StatsManager/get_configuration first and supply the complete intended domain/analyzer set for this account. Round-trip enabled_by_user, the user choice, into input enabled; enabled in the read result is the effective administrator/user state. Analyzers absent from the read receive their defaults. A partial-looking input can reset other settings to defaults. The client performs no implicit read, merge, patch, retry, restore or rollback.

On cPanel 11.138.0.19 the handler builds defaults for every domain/analyzer, applies supplied changes, then saves. Unspecified configurations receive defaults; the POD describes them as disabled. Do not assume every default is universally disabled.

Available in cPanel 90 and later; disabled when the WebServer role is disabled. Root/reseller-controlled analyzers cannot be managed by the cPanel user. This is one direct-UAPI JSON POST; WHM-bridged UAPI is refused locally after metadata reset.

Configuration and every listed member are required. changes must be nonempty and domain must be a non-empty string; analyzers may be empty and an analyzer name may be empty. Strings are forwarded without trimming or hostname validation. Structural validity does not prove account completeness, ownership, analyzer availability or persistence.

Input enabled requires native bool and maps to integer 0/1. Names remain strings without a closed analyzer enum. On cPanel 11.138.0.19 save and get return the same analyzer row: name, enabled and enabled_by_user. All response fields remain optional and flags remain native integer 0/1. Additional analyzer information stays in responseMeta()->uapi[metadata]: available_for_user is an analyzer setting, and locked=1 permits only reseller/root management while locked=0 permits user management.

On cPanel 11.138.0.19 status 1 can accompany skipped entries and warnings for not_owned, not_available or unrecognized entries. An empty analyzer name produces an unrecognized warning; an empty domain is skipped without a warning by the upstream handler and is rejected locally. Inspect responseMeta() warnings and verify persistence separately; success does not establish that every requested setting applied.
